test_title: PYST 43: SSC CPO - English Comprehension (Held on 11 Nov 2022 Shift 3)
subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

To judge a book by its cover

options.text: To be good at evaluating people
To evaluate people’s worth by their outward appearance

solution:
The correct answer is **To evaluate people’s worth by their outward appearance**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate **meaning **of the given idiom '**To judge a book by its cover**' is '**To evaluate people's worth by their outward appearance'**.
 
• **To judge a book by its cover**: you shouldn't judge someone or something based only on what you see on the outside or only on what you perceive without knowing the full situation.
 
 
• E.g. *That man may look very small and insignificant, but don't judge a book by its cover – he's a very powerful man in his circle.*
 
 

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's look at more idioms with similar meanings.
 
 
• **Beauty is only skin deep**- My mother always used to say that beauty is only skin-deep. What's really important is the sort of person you are.
 
• **All that glitters is not gold**- Try to remember that all that glitters is not gold, so be careful if parting with money.

 
 
• **Appearance is deceptive**- Appearances are deceptive. It is not possible to judge a person's character from their outward appearance.
